title: Control Bay: Navigation synthesis and Command Lens prototypes for console IA
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The current console navigation mixes global controls, per-project routes, and rollout/cost surfaces in ways that increase cognitive load for engineers and platform teams. Scope: synthesize a single navigation paradigm ("Control Bay") that reduces deep click paths, surfaces rollout and cost signals earlier, and adapts to user role. Deliverables: 3 high-fidelity Figma prototypes (Global Command Lens, Focused Project Strip, Rollout & Cost Quickcards), annotated IA map, interaction specs for pinned lanes and contextual breadcrumbs, and a usability test plan for 20 sessions. Goals: 1) cut average route depth to critical dashboards by 30%, 2) reduce time-to-find rollout policies by 40%, 3) provide clear affordances for switching deployment mode (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with minimal friction.
comments: 2025-11-12 Asha: Kickoff notes - aligned with PM on problem statement; product wants an approach that works with both small teams and enterprise RBAC. Identified primary personas: quick-ops engineer, platform SRE, product manager monitoring costs.

2025-11-14 Renata: Initial sketches uploaded to Figma (link below). Explored three metaphors: strip-based project lanes, stacked lenses, and a compact command pallet. Favored approach: Command Lens (single persistent left column that morphs by context).

2025-11-16 PM (Liam O'Connor): Feedback - prioritize discoverability for rollouts and cost alerts. Request: add a compact cost delta chip on every project row and a one-click view to open cost breakdown.

2025-11-17 Eng (Marcus Lee): Feasibility note - suggested implementation via route-level metadata and a small nav-state API; flagged performance impact for servers with 200+ projects. Suggested server-side prefetching for active lens items.
2025-11-18 Asha: Usability script drafted; recruiting criteria set (mix of infra engineers, ML engineers, product owners). Metrics: task success, time on task, click depth, subjective SUS score.
2025-11-19 Renata: Updated Figma prototypes (v2) with accessibility contrast adjustments and a keyboard-first flow; added localized label lengths for worst-case languages.
2025-11-20 PM (Liam): Approved for lab testing pending small copy edits and Eng acceptance of nav-state API contract.
2025-11-20 Eng (Marcus): Proposed dependency ticket ENG-21098 for nav-state API. Blocking until ENG-21098 is scheduled.
2025-11-20 Asha: Marking this ticket In Review. Usability sessions scheduled starting 2025-11-24; will capture first-run metrics and iterate.
decisions: Adopt 'Control Bay' as the umbrella IA pattern: a persistent left command lens plus a dynamic center canvas.
Expose cost deltas as micro-chips on project rows (hover expands to quickcard).
Enable direct keyboard command palette (CMD+K) entry points mapped to top-level lens routes.
Do not collapse project context into a single dropdown; instead surface project strips to reduce context switches.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototypes delivered for the three variants with interaction specs and edge states.
Annotated IA map with canonical routes and fallback patterns for low-permission users.
Usability pilot completed (>=16 usable sessions) with documented metrics and at least two actionable design changes.
Engineering sign-off on nav-state contract (or alternative implementation plan) and a dependency ticket created.
next_steps: Finalize copy and microcopy for cost chips and rollout badges (owner: PM).
Run 20 moderated usability sessions (owner: Design Research).
Coordinate with Eng to create ENG-21098 (nav-state API) and agree on feature flags for progressive rollout.
Prepare implementation handoff package: tokens, components, CSS tokens, and interaction docs.
